{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABYix4qQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhCHdsc", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 11, "title": "Implement complete baseline Sega Saturn CPUs and built-in hardware emulation", "body": "## Problem

The current saturn-rust implementation is a deliberately narrow, independently written Saturn hardware subset that runs the original Star Collector homebrew. It is **not yet a general-purpose Sega Saturn emulator**. In particular, the interpreter implements only selected SH-2 instructions; the slave SH-2 and sound 68EC000 are absent; VDP2 and SMPC support only the paths used by the homebrew; and VDP1, SCU, SCSP, a functional runtime CD block, full BIOS services, native BIOS boot, interrupts, timers, DMA and system-level synchronization remain incomplete or missing.

The request is to **finish a comprehensive baseline implementation of the standard Sega Saturn hardware in one overarching Issue**, rather than close successive small feature Issues. The deliverable is a cohesive, independently implemented Rust emulation system that runs in WebAssembly with substantially general functionality, not a collection of stubs optimized for one game.

## Expected outcome

Implement, integrate, document and test the **complete documented architectural instruction sets and the major built-in retail Saturn subsystems**: both SH-2 processors, sound MC68EC000, system bus and memories, SCU (including DMA, interrupt controller and DSP), SMPC, VDP1, VDP2, SCSP (including its DSP), CD block, backup RAM and system timing. Support real user-supplied BIOS as well as an independently written BIOS-less HLE path. The emulator should be able to execute **multiple independent Saturn-targeted programs** exercising different hardware paths, and offer a usable browser interface on GitHub Pages.

**Scope rule: this is ONE end-to-end completion Issue.** Internal milestones and multiple implementation PRs are allowed, but any incomplete PR must explicitly leave this Issue open. **Do not close this Issue** because a single CPU or device starts working, a test homebrew plays, or an arbitrary percentage of the work is done. Closure requires the full, evidence-backed acceptance criteria below.

“Comprehensive baseline” means implementing the documented programming model and functional behaviors of all listed **built-in** subsystems, with conformance testing, not guaranteeing cycle-perfect analog/electrical behavior or 100% compatibility with every commercial game. Unsupported documented standard-hardware features must be listed as outstanding failures, rather than silently stubbed, before claiming completion. Optional peripherals and optimization work are explicitly out of scope at the bottom.

## Context and reproduction

This is planned new functionality; reproduction steps are not applicable. At drafting, current main contains:

- CPU: src/cpu.rs — partial master SH-2 interpreter, delayed branches and deterministic errors.
- Bus: src/bus.rs — partial RAM, BIOS, VDP2 and SMPC memory map.
- Devices: src/devices.rs — restricted VDP2 RGB bitmap and SMPC digital pad direct access.
- Disc: src/disc.rs — bounded ISO9660/Saturn IP parser and simple first-read HLE disc boot; no runtime CD command system.
- Machine: src/lib.rs — one CPU, bounded instruction-count scheduling rather than hardware cycle/event scheduling.
- Wasm/browser: src/wasm.rs, web/ — working Play/Debug interface, local file input and GitHub Pages deployment.
- Existing original MIT-licensed guest: homebrew/star-collector — retain its functionality and tests.

Inspect the latest main again before changing anything. Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md), and [existing architecture](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/architecture.md). Write PRs, Issues, engineering documentation and commits in English.

### Primary engineering references

Use the original manuals as the authority; document section references and discrepancies, and add test fixtures for discovered behavior:

- [Saturn original manuals archive and index](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs): Saturn Overview / Dual CPU User's Guide; Hitachi SH-1/SH-2 Programming Manual and SH7604 Hardware Manual; Sega SCU, SCU DSP, SMPC, VDP1, VDP2, SCSP, CD Block, Boot ROM, Disc Format and System Program/Backup documentation; Motorola M68000 Programmer's Reference Manual.
- [Sega's Saturn hardware manual collection](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/index.htm).
- [Historical Sega documentation catalog](https://www.segasaturnshiro.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/DTS-Vol-3-No-2-Jun-95.pdf).

Reference emulators can be used for **independent differential observations** but do not copy or transliterate their CPU/device/HLE cores, lookup tables, code or proprietary SDK material. Keep an implementation/source provenance record. Ordinary build/Wasm/UI/testing libraries are acceptable; processor emulation libraries and third-party emulator cores are not. Keep the existing clean-room approach.

## Required technical scope

### 1. CPU cores: two Hitachi SH-2 + sound MC68EC000

- Complete the **documented SH-2 architectural instruction set**, covering every valid instruction family, addressing mode, flags (SR/T/Q/M), MAC/saturation, multiply/divide, shifts/rotates, bit operations, branches and delay slots, PC-relative access, system/control-register transfers, privileged behavior, sleep, traps and exceptions. Implement illegal-instruction and slot-illegal errors according to SH-2 semantics; remove host-only “unsupported opcode” for documented valid opcodes.
- Implement both master and slave **independent** SH-2 states with documented startup/reset, shared memory/bus visibility, inter-CPU signaling, interrupt prioritization, vector/stack entry and return, and the essential SH7604 on-chip peripherals: cache/address aliasing, interrupt controller, free-running timer, watchdog, serial/DMA/bus interfaces and relevant internal mapped registers. Explicitly model instruction/data effects where timing or cache coherency is software-visible.
- Independently implement the **MC68EC000** architecture for Saturn sound CPU use: its documented applicable 68000 instructions, effective-address modes, flags, supervisor/user state, exception vectors, interrupts, stack behavior, reset, and access to sound RAM and SCSP register bus. No external 68k core.
- Make all three processor traces reproducible and inspectable from deterministic test fixtures. The existing debugger may grow selectively, but do not bury correctness behind a JIT. The interpreter remains the reference executor.

### 2. Complete base-system mapping and event-driven synchronization

- Expand the documented retail Saturn physical/address map and access rules: BIOS ROM, SMPC/RTC, battery-backed backup RAM, both work RAM banks and mirrors, cartridge/A-bus address decoding needed for base access, sound RAM, SCSP, VDP1 VRAM/frame buffers/controls, VDP2 VRAM/CRAM/registers, SCU, CD block, SH-2 internal regions, and byte/word/long access and invalid-access behavior. Cartridge accessories are separately scoped below; unmapped address regions must not masquerade as implemented devices.
- Replace instruction-count-only “frames” with a **deterministic shared event/time scheduler** coordinating dual SH-2, 68k, video scanlines/hblank/vblank, audio sample generation, DMA, timers, interrupts, SMPC commands and CD events. Respect documented clock-domain relationships, ordering, memory visibility, and software-observable contention/waits; document remaining non-cycle-accurate approximations.
- Distinguish power-on, hard/soft reset, slave CPU start/stop, sound CPU start/stop, initial state, interrupt acknowledgment, and persistent backup RAM semantics. Ensure stalled/waiting CPUs do not deadlock the UI.
- Maintain bounded execution and error handling in Wasm. No unbounded browser main-thread loop; let emulated audio/video advance consistently. Web Workers/JIT are **not** needed for correctness and are not required by this Issue.

### 3. SCU, DMA, interrupt control, DSP

- Implement the documented SCU register model, interrupt requests/masks/priorities/vectors, A-bus/B-bus access coordination, all SCU DMA channels with direct/indirect operations, transfer increments, triggers, completion/errors and interactions with VRAM/sound/CD buffers.
- Implement the SCU **DSP** programming model and instruction behavior, registers, memory/data transfers and execution control (independently; no imported DSP core). Provide deterministic DSP programs and DMA tests. No perpetual no-op DSP stub.

### 4. VDP1 + VDP2 video pipeline

- VDP1: command list parsing/control flow, normal/scaled/distorted sprites, polygons, polylines/lines, clipping, local coordinate system, sprite color/texture formats, palette modes, transparency/shadow/half-luminance and Gouraud shading, drawing order, framebuffer access, erase/swap, end/status/interrupt behavior. Use device register and VRAM data, not per-game host rendering.
- VDP2: VRAM banking/cycle patterns and CRAM, NBG0–NBG3 and rotating backgrounds, character/tile and bitmap modes, scrolling/zoom, line/vertical-cell effects, windows, mosaic, priority/composition, sprite priority/color calculation with VDP1, transparency/color offset/blending/shadow and display modes including relevant PAL/NTSC, resolutions, interlace and blanking behavior.
- The combined output must be derived from emulated VRAM/registers and yield stable testable pixels for independent guest programs, including overlapping VDP1/VDP2 elements and mixed priority/transparency scenarios. Keep nearest-neighbor and aspect-ratio handling in the frontend; avoid hardcoded game-specific images.

### 5. Audio: 68EC000, SCSP and CD-DA

- With the 68k core above, implement SCSP sound RAM/register interface, 32 sound slots, PCM (8/16-bit) and FM-related modes, envelope, looping, pitch modulation, LFO, per-voice level/pan, timers, interrupt dispatch, MIDI registers/behavior relevant to built-in hardware, DMA and the **SCSP effects DSP** instruction/routing model.
- Generate correctly paced stereo samples in Rust and stream to browser output (e.g. AudioWorklet with a bounded buffer); handle muted/unavailable user-gesture audio and underflow gracefully. Audio-only state must be testable without browser speakers.
- Route supported CD-DA tracks to the SCSP external audio input/mixer. Do not silently discard audio commands or report successful playback while producing no samples.

### 6. CD subsystem, BIOS and media

- Implement the documented **CD block host-visible command/status/HIRQ interface**, TOC and sessions/tracks, sector reading and buffering, filter/selector/partition operations, data transfers, seeks/spin state as needed for software-observable behavior, and CD-DA. The block's internal SH-1/firmware can be independently behaviorally emulated (HLE) rather than running proprietary internal firmware, but the SH-2-facing contract must be covered by documented tests.
- Support the practical disc-image formats necessary to exercise standard Saturn discs: cooked ISO (existing), **BIN/CUE** with raw 2352-byte sectors, track layout/pregaps and mixed data/audio discs. Validate size, bounds, format, CUE references and file errors; no uploads or server-only image processing. CHD/compressed formats are optional.
- Keep **both boot modes**: (a) local **user-supplied genuine BIOS** executes from its real reset vectors and initializes the machine without secretly falling back to HLE; (b) independently implemented **BIOS-less HLE** for startup and documented system/backup/CD-related BIOS service calls used by supported software. Document per-call ABI/side effects and version/region differences; do not copy Sega firmware. The legacy narrow HLE fixture can remain as an explicit debug mode.
- Provide evidence of functional native BIOS path beyond merely reading reset vectors: successful BIOS initialization/menu or a documented BIOS-driven boot scenario with a lawfully supplied BIOS. Automated CI must use original/synthetic BIOS fixtures and **must never embed a Sega BIOS**. A licensed local real-BIOS integration check is necessary before claiming native BIOS compatibility; explain access requirements and record non-sensitive results, not BIOS bytes.
- Implement backup memory hardware and a safe per-user browser export/import or equivalent explicit persistence mechanism appropriate to the project's local-file privacy guarantees; no network or automatic media upload.

### 7. SMPC, controllers and remaining built-in peripheral behavior

- Implement SMPC command sequencing, state/status registers, reset and power control, RTC handling, INTBACK reporting, region/system flags, controller port polling and interrupts with realistic guest-visible latency/order.
- Support both standard digital controller ports, keyboard mappings and at least the documented commonly used analog-pad input mode. Ensure input is routed through emulated hardware registers/SMPC commands, never direct game-memory writes. Do not regress the existing Play/Debug focus and held-key release logic.
- Model any other **built-in, software-visible** interfaces necessary for standard base-console operation and boot, with documented register coverage and test evidence. Optional physical accessories (modem/NetLink, light guns, MPEG/video-CD card, multitaps, 4 MB expansion RAM, special cartridges) are **not** mandatory for this base-console completion Issue unless an explicit dependency is discovered and documented.

## Evidence and integration strategy

This is intentionally **one large Issue, not a sequence of separate closed feature Issues**. Work may proceed in as many coherent PRs as needed, but the Issue stays open until all sections have working implementations and tests.

Maintain a living **hardware conformance matrix** in docs (one row per SH-2/68k instruction family and each major documented device feature/register group): manual reference, implemented behavior, edge cases, native automated test, browser/integration test, and any known limitation. A box checked solely because a register is accepted and ignored is **not implemented**. Keep a concrete unresolved-gaps list and update it with every PR.

Required integration examples must be **genuine guest code** running under the cores (no host-created pseudo-game logic):

1. Preserve **Star Collector** intact (HLE disc boot, SMPC input, VDP2 frame output, score/finish/restart and browser tests).
2. Add a second **independently authored, openly licensed, reproducibly built Saturn-targeted program/disc** using materially different hardware, at minimum VDP1 command rendering + VDP2 composition and real audio generated by guest-controlled SCSP/68k.
3. Add original deterministic guest tests or another redistributable disc covering **both SH-2 CPUs, SCU DMA/interrupts and runtime CD sector access**, with observable memory/IRQ/output results.
4. Add test harness fixtures covering the SCU DSP, SCSP DSP, representative line/rotation/window/priority video cases, BIOS HLE calls, reset and backup RAM behavior. These can be small programs rather than additional full games.

Prefer openly licensed third-party homebrew for independent compatibility evidence only where source/assets/build products have been individually audited. Otherwise create original test software with clear redistribution grants. This Issue must not depend on pirated commercial games or on copying SDK objects, firmware or third-party emulator code.

Run differential traces/reference-image/audio comparisons where legally possible, but independently authored test vectors based on primary manuals and emulator-driven assertions must be sufficient for CI. Report verification limits rather than inventing commercial compatibility percentages.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Instruction coverage:** documented valid SH-2 architectural opcodes/variants and applicable MC68EC000 instructions have executable correctness tests covering addressing, flags, faults/exceptions/interrupts and control flow; SCU DSP and SCSP DSP have executable opcode/register tests. No known valid opcode remains a generic “unsupported” failure in the supported architectural scope.
- [ ] **Multiprocessor/scheduler:** master/slave SH-2 and 68k execute independently and exchange guest-visible data/interrupts through an event/time scheduler; deterministic tests cover interleaving, cache visibility, timers, priority and reset without hardcoded per-game behavior.
- [ ] **Bus and SCU:** base-console maps, mirrors, alignment/width effects, MMIO side effects, backup RAM, SCU DMA/interrupts and DSP are exercised by independent read/write/IRQ/transfer tests.
- [ ] **Video:** independent guest test scenes exercise VDP1 primitives and command/state changes, VDP2 tile/bitmap/rotation/window/scroll/color behavior, compositing and display timing, with stable expected pixel or framebuffer-hash outputs and documented coverage.
- [ ] **Sound:** 68k-driven SCSP PCM/FM slot, envelope/timer/IRQ/effects DSP and CD-DA paths produce measurable, deterministic stereo sample buffers; an actual guest program produces non-silent, correctly directed output in the browser after audio is enabled.
- [ ] **CD/boot:** realistic CD block command/IRQ/sector tests cover cooked ISO and BIN/CUE including audio/data tracks and invalid media; HLE boots the original discs and documented BIOS service fixtures. The independent native-BIOS path is demonstrably beyond reset vectors using a lawfully obtained BIOS in local verification; firmware is never committed or transmitted.
- [ ] **SMPC/input/system:** both ports, digital and common analog input, INTBACK/system commands/RTC/reset and save backup memory are testable by guest-level reads, and player input never mutates guest memory through host shortcuts.
- [ ] **Hardware coverage document:** a manual-linked, current conformance matrix exists for all required subsystems. No required device is merely stubbed or silently ignored; no unmet required feature is marked complete. Known approximations are explicit and have regression tests where externally observable.
- [ ] **Independent integration:** Star Collector remains playable and unchanged in behavior; the second licensed game/test disc demonstrates distinct VDP1+VDP2 and guest-controlled audio; further test programs independently validate dual-CPU/SCU/CD and DSP paths. All run in **native and Wasm** environments using guest code and simulated controllers, without a proprietary ROM.
- [ ] **Browser compatibility:** Play/Debug, image and BIOS local selection, player controls, keyboard focus safety, fullscreen behavior and GitHub Pages /saturn-rust/ asset delivery continue working. Sustained emulator execution cannot permanently block the browser event loop. Do not require a particular FPS benchmark for correctness.
- [ ] **Regression/build validation:** documented cargo fmt/build/test/clippy commands, Wasm build, ISO/game reproducibility checks and real Chromium/Playwright browser tests all pass in CI; record actual results and any skipped checks. No copied emulator cores, unauthorized files or prohibited media enter the repository/public site.
- [ ] **Scope integrity:** all the requested built-in systems above are implemented and reviewed; additional PRs may be merged partially but **this Issue is closed only when this entire list is met**, not merely when one homebrew or a BIOS screen works.

## Optional validation

- Compare with lawful physical Saturn output or independent reference-emulator traces across more games and regional BIOS variants.
- Validate in Firefox/Safari/mobile, add additional licensed demos and measure baseline speed/latency.
- Implement CHD support, optional cartridges/peripherals, micro-timing refinements beyond the documented software-visible requirements, Web Workers, predecoded interpreter, SH-2-to-Wasm dynamic recompilation, SIMD or other performance optimizations **in separate follow-up work**. Do not replace correctness with speed work.

## Required post-merge verification

After the PR that fully satisfies this Issue is merged and GitHub Pages deploys, verify the public https://takahirox.github.io/saturn-rust/ build, boot/BIOS selection, independent homebrew demonstrations, video, audio, input, Debug view and locally loaded permitted media. Record the deployed commit, successful workflow and any production-only findings. This real-site check occurs **after** merge and must not be misrepresented as pre-merge validation.

This task is large by design. If only part is completed, preserve the Issue as open, explicitly report which required items are still missing, and do not relabel the implementation as a complete Saturn emulator.
